fields.families[].lichess: lichess name prefixes; a lichess name belongs to the family/variation with the LONGEST matching prefix, matched at a component boundary (end of string, ": " or ", ")
fields.families[].side: who chooses it: white | black | both (curated; overrides move-parity attribution)
fields.families[].tier: 1 very common at club level on lichess, 2 common, 3 occasional (estimated; explorer.lichess.ovh was not reachable from the sandbox)
fields.families[].generic: placeholder name (1.e4 / 1.d4 / 1.Nf3 / 1.d4 Nf6 / 2.Nf3): never announce as a choice, wait for a specific family
fields.families[].umbrella: family this one answers (QGD/QGA/Slav/Semi-Slav/Tarrasch/Chigorin/Albin -> queens_gambit; KGA/KGD -> kings_gambit): White's opening is the umbrella, Black's defence this family
fields.names.<lang>.name: citation form (subtitles, title case where the language uses it)
fields.names.<lang>.def: form with the definite article, for sentence templates (en/fr/de/es; ar, ru, uk, ja, zh need none)
fields.names.<lang>.gender: grammatical gender (fr/de/es: m f n; ru/uk: m f n) for agreement in templates
fields.comment: English source text, beginner and advanced; translators render it; <=2 sentences each
fields.review: languages whose name should be checked by a native chess player before shipping
fields.glossary: generic words of lichess components with per-language composition patterns ({X} proper name, {Xgen} genitive for ru/uk)
fields.eponyms: proper names that appear in many variation names, transliterated (ru/uk nominative + genitive)
fields.ignore_components: lichess components never spoken (uninformative); also ignore any component that starts with "with " or contains a move (regex [KQRBN]?[a-h]?x?[a-h][1-8]|O-O)

comment.beginner: 1.e4 grabs the centre and opens lines for the queen and the king's bishop at once; it is the most popular first move at every level.
comment.advanced: 1.e4 leads to open, tactical play after 1...e5 and to sharp, unbalanced fights against the Sicilian, French or Caro-Kann; everything revolves around the e4 pawn and fast development.

pt.name: Abertura do Peão da Dama

comment.beginner: 1.d4 takes the centre with a pawn that the queen already protects; the games are usually slower and more strategic than after 1.e4.
comment.advanced: Queen's pawn openings lead to closed or semi-closed positions where piece placement, pawn structure and the c4 and e4 levers matter more than early tactics.

es.name: Apertura del caballo de rey
es.def: la apertura del caballo de rey

ja.name: キングズ・ナイト・オープニング

pt-BR.name: Abertura do Cavalo do Rei
pt-BR.def: a Abertura do Cavalo do Rei

pt.name: Abertura do Cavalo do Rei
pt.def: a Abertura do Cavalo do Rei

comment.beginner: The knight comes out while attacking the e5 pawn: the most natural move in the open games, and Black usually defends with 2...Nc6.
comment.advanced: 2.Nf3 keeps every classical option (Ruy Lopez, Italian, Scotch, Four Knights) and makes Black commit to a defence of e5: ...Nc6, ...d6 or the ...Nf6 counterattack.

ja.name: シシリアン・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black answers 1.e4 with the c-pawn instead of the e-pawn and creates an unbalanced position: expect a sharp game where each side attacks on its own wing.
comment.advanced: After d4 and cxd4 Black trades a wing pawn for a centre pawn, gaining the half-open c-file and a central majority, while White gets a lead in development and kingside attacking chances, often with castling on opposite sides.

ja.name: フレンチ・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black prepares ...d5 with ...e6: a solid defence, but the bishop on c8 is often shut in behind its own pawns.
comment.advanced: When White plays e5 a locked pawn chain appears: White attacks on the kingside, Black undermines the chain with ...c5 and ...f6, and the light-squared bishop remains Black's problem piece.

ja.name: カロ・カン・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black prepares ...d5 with ...c6 and keeps the c8 bishop free: a very solid defence with few weaknesses.
comment.advanced: The Caro-Kann gives Black a healthy structure and an active light-squared bishop (...Bf5 or ...Bg4); White usually takes space (Advance) or a small lead in development, while Black aims for a timely ...c5 or a good endgame.

ja.name: スカンジナビアン・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black hits the e4 pawn at once with ...d5; when the queen recaptures, White gains time by attacking her, so Black must know where she belongs (a5 or d6).
comment.advanced: The Scandinavian reaches a Caro-Kann-like structure with the light bishop outside the pawn chain; White keeps a small edge in space and development, Black gets a solid, easy-to-learn setup.

ja.name: イタリアン・ゲーム

comment.beginner: White develops the bishop to c4, aiming at the weak f7 square: a classical opening where both sides develop quickly and castle.
comment.advanced: Modern Italian games are slow manoeuvring battles with c3 and d3 that prepare d4 later; sharper tries are the Evans Gambit and the Two Knights lines with Ng5.

ja.name: ルイ・ロペス

comment.beginner: White's bishop attacks the knight that defends e5: one of the oldest and deepest openings, rich in slow strategic play.
comment.advanced: The Ruy Lopez builds long-term pressure on e5 and the centre: the c3-d4 centre, the knight tour Nbd2-f1-g3 and Black's queenside expansion with ...a6 and ...b5, with sharp sidelines such as the Marshall Attack.

ja.name: スコッチ・ゲーム

comment.beginner: White opens the centre at once with d4: the pieces come out fast and the position becomes open early.
comment.advanced: The Scotch releases the central tension immediately; after 4.Nxd4 the play turns on Black's active development (...Bc5 or ...Nf6) and on structures such as the doubled c-pawns after Nxc6.

ja.name: フィリドール・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black defends e5 with a pawn (...d6): solid but a little passive, because the f8 bishop is shut in.
comment.advanced: The Philidor concedes space for a firm grip on e5 (the Hanham setup ...Nd7, ...Be7, ...c6); White gets comfortable central pressure, and tricks against f7 are common at club level.

ja.name: ペトロフ・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black does not defend e5 but counterattacks e4 with the knight: a solid, symmetrical defence; just don't copy White's moves for too long.
comment.advanced: The Petrov leads to symmetrical and often drawish structures; White keeps a small initiative, Black develops quickly and aims for equalising exchanges. The trappy Stafford Gambit is an offshoot.

families.note: Russian usage prefers "Русская партия"; Ukrainian text uses "Захист Петрова" on purpose.

es.name: Apertura de los cuatro caballos
es.def: la apertura de los cuatro caballos

ja.name: フォー・ナイツ・ゲーム

comment.beginner: Both sides bring out their knights first: a sound, quiet opening that follows the rules of development.
comment.advanced: The Four Knights is symmetrical and balanced; White chooses a Spanish (Bb5), Scotch (d4) or Italian (Bc4) treatment, and Black should know the Rubinstein counter-gambit and the Halloween Gambit.

ja.name: イングリッシュ・オープニング

comment.beginner: White starts with the c-pawn instead of a centre pawn and controls d5 from the side: a flexible opening where the centre is fought for with pieces.
comment.advanced: The English often transposes to 1.d4 openings; its own lines (Symmetrical, Reversed Sicilian with ...e5) lead to fianchetto manoeuvring, pressure on d5 and queenside play.

ja.name: ツケルトート・オープニング

comment.beginner: 1.Nf3 develops a piece and watches the centre without committing a pawn yet.
comment.advanced: 1.Nf3 is a move-order tool: it can become a Réti, English, Catalan or Queen's Gambit while avoiding some Black systems such as the Budapest or early Dutch lines.

ja.name: クイーンズ・ギャンビット

comment.beginner: White offers the c-pawn to pull Black's d-pawn away from the centre; it is not a real sacrifice, because White can usually win the pawn back.
comment.advanced: c4 attacks the d5 strongpoint; Black chooses between holding it (Declined, Slav) and giving it up for free development (Accepted), with minority attacks and isolated d-pawn middlegames as typical themes.

ja.name: クイーンズ・ギャンビット・ディクラインド

comment.beginner: Black keeps a pawn on d5 and supports it with ...e6: very solid, but the light-squared bishop on c8 needs care.
comment.advanced: Classical structures: the Carlsbad after cxd5 exd5 with White's minority attack, Black freeing the game with ...c5 or ...e5, and the eternal question of the c8 bishop; the Orthodox, Tartakower and Lasker defences are the main lines.

ja.name: クイーンズ・ギャンビット・アクセプテッド

comment.beginner: Black takes the offered pawn but does not try to keep it: the point is to develop freely and hit White's centre with ...c5.
comment.advanced: White regains c4 and often ends up with an isolated d-pawn after ...c5 and exchanges on d4; the game is about piece activity against a long-term structural weakness.

ja.name: スラヴ・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black supports d5 with ...c6 and keeps the c8 bishop free to come out: a very solid defence.
comment.advanced: The Slav holds d5 without locking in the light bishop; main lines revolve around ...dxc4 with ...Bf5 or ...Bg4 against White's a4 and e4 plans, or the symmetrical Exchange Slav.

ja.name: セミスラヴ・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black combines the Slav pawn (...c6) with the Queen's Gambit Declined pawn (...e6): it looks quiet but leads to very sharp lines.
comment.advanced: The Semi-Slav branches into the Meran (...dxc4 and ...b5 queenside expansion) and the ultra-sharp Botvinnik and Moscow gambits; Black's c8 bishop often finds b7 after ...b5.

ja.name: インディアン・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black answers 1.d4 with the knight instead of a pawn and keeps options open: the gateway to all the "Indian" defences.
comment.advanced: 1...Nf6 stops e4 for now and delays Black's pawn commitment; the next move (...g6, ...e6 or ...c5) chooses between King's Indian or Grünfeld, Nimzo or Queen's Indian, and Benoni or Benko structures.

ja.name: キングズ・インディアン・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black lets White build a big centre, puts the bishop on g7, then strikes back: a dynamic fighting defence.
comment.advanced: Black concedes space and then hits the centre with ...e5 or ...c5; once the centre is closed with d5, White attacks on the queenside with c5 while Black storms the kingside with ...f5, ...f4 and ...g5.

families.note: lichess names the position after 3.Nc3 "King's Indian Defense" (parity would give it to White): the curated side is authoritative.

lichess: Queen's Pawn Game: Accelerated London System

ja.name: ロンドン・システム

comment.beginner: White sets up d4, Bf4, e3, Nf3 and c3 against almost anything: easy to learn, solid, with a clear plan.
comment.advanced: A stable pyramid (d4-e3-c3) with the bishop outside the chain; White plays for a kingside initiative with Ne5 and h4 or for a slow squeeze, and Black's most testing replies are an early ...c5 and ...Qb6 against b2.

ja.name: モダン・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black puts the king's bishop on g7 with ...g6 and lets White take the centre, planning to attack it later.
comment.advanced: The Modern (Robatsch) is hypermodern and flexible: Black delays ...Nf6 and keeps ...c6, ...a6-b5 or ...e5 in reserve; White can build a big centre or go for f4 or a Be3-Qd2 attack.

ja.name: ピルツ・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black plays ...d6, ...Nf6 and ...g6 and lets White build a centre, then counters it: a flexible fighting defence.
comment.advanced: White gets a broad centre; the main battles are the Austrian Attack (f4) and the Be3-Qd2 attacks, while Black strikes with ...c5 or ...e5 and relies on the g7 bishop.

ja.name: ウィーン・ゲーム

comment.beginner: White develops the queen's knight first and often follows with f4: a lively opening with quick attacking chances.
comment.advanced: The Vienna prepares f4 (the Vienna Gambit) or a quiet g3 or Bc4 setup; Black's main answer is ...Nf6 with ...d5 counterplay, and the Frankenstein-Dracula line is famous for its complications.

ja.name: ビショップス・オープニング

comment.beginner: White develops the bishop to c4 before the knight, aiming at f7 and keeping the f-pawn free.
comment.advanced: A flexible move order that often transposes to the Italian or the Vienna; independent lines include the Urusov Gambit (d4) and quiet d3 setups.

ja.name: アレヒン・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black attacks e4 with the knight to lure White's pawns forward: they gain space but can become targets.
comment.advanced: The Alekhine invites e5 and pawn chases (the Four Pawns Attack), then undermines the overextended centre with ...d6, ...c5 or ...Bg4; the Modern Variation with 4.Nf3 is the calm main line.

ja.name: キングズ・ギャンビット

comment.beginner: White sacrifices the f-pawn to open the f-file and take the centre: a romantic attacking opening from the nineteenth century.
comment.advanced: White trades a pawn for central control and the f-file; Black can keep the pawn with ...g5 (very sharp), return it with ...d5, or decline with ...Bc5 or the Falkbeer ...d5.

ja.name: キングズ・ギャンビット・アクセプテッド

comment.beginner: Black takes the f-pawn: the game becomes very sharp, and both kings are a little exposed.
comment.advanced: Black either tries to hold the pawn with ...g5 (Kieseritzky and Muzio territory) or gives it back for quick development with ...d5 or ...Nf6; White relies on the f-file and a lead in development.

ja.name: キングズ・ギャンビット・ディクラインド

comment.beginner: Black refuses the pawn and develops instead, often with ...Bc5, which stops White from castling short for a while.
comment.advanced: ...Bc5 keeps the g1-a7 diagonal under pressure and the Falkbeer (...d5) strikes back in the centre; both avoid the long forcing theory of the accepted lines.

ja.name: ニムゾヴィッチ・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black answers 1.e4 with the queen's knight: an unusual but playable defence that often transposes to other openings.
comment.advanced: 1...Nc6 invites 2.d4 d5 or ...e5 structures, or transposes to open games after 2.Nf3 e5; its independent value lies in surprise and flexible piece play.

families.note: ru/uk "Защита Нимцовича" is also the usual name of the Nimzo-Indian; say "1...Кc6" in subtitles when both could be meant.

ja.name: オーウェン・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black puts the queen's bishop on b7 to hit e4 from afar; White should simply take the centre.
comment.advanced: A hypermodern setup (...b6, ...Bb7, ...e6) that concedes the centre early; White gains space and must watch the long diagonal.

ja.name: ホロヴィッツ・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black plays ...e6 against 1.d4 and keeps options open: it usually turns into a French, a Queen's Gambit Declined or a Dutch.
comment.advanced: 1...e6 is a transpositional move order; its own lines are the Kangaroo (...Bb4+) and English Defence setups with ...b6.

ja.name: ファント・クライス・オープニング

comment.beginner: 1.e3 opens the bishop's diagonal but takes little of the centre: a quiet start, usually followed by d4 or c4.
comment.advanced: 1.e3 usually transposes into reversed French, Colle or Stonewall setups; it hands Black the fight for the centre at no real risk.

ja.name: センター・ゲーム

comment.beginner: White opens the centre with d4 on move two, but after the exchange the queen recaptures early and can be chased.
comment.advanced: Black develops with tempo against the queen (...Nc6); White usually plays Qe3, Nc3, Bd2 and castles long for an attack.

ja.name: エングルンド・ギャンビット

comment.beginner: Black offers the e-pawn against 1.d4 and hopes for traps; objectively dubious, but dangerous if White does not know it.
comment.advanced: The Englund (1...e5 2.dxe5 Nc6) relies on tricks such as ...Qe7 and ...Qb4+; White keeps a sound extra pawn with Nf3, Bf4 and careful development.

ja.name: ダッチ・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black plays ...f5 against 1.d4 to control e4 and aim at the kingside: ambitious, but it loosens Black's king a little.
comment.advanced: The Dutch leads to Leningrad (...g6), Stonewall (...d5, ...e6, ...c6) or Classical (...e6, ...d6) setups; Black fights for e4 and a kingside attack, White aims at e4 and the weakened e6 square.

ja.name: ニムゾ・インディアン・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black pins the c3 knight with the bishop to stop e4: a highly respected defence that often leaves White with doubled pawns.
comment.advanced: Black gives bishop for knight to control e4 and damage White's structure; White gets the bishop pair and central potential (Rubinstein e3, Classical Qc2, Sämisch a3).

ja.name: クイーンズ・インディアン・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black puts the queen's bishop on b7 to control the central light squares: solid and flexible.
comment.advanced: Black fights for e4 and d5 with pieces; typical ideas are ...Ba6 against c4, Hedgehog setups and the ...c5 or ...d5 breaks, against White's g3 or a3 systems.

ja.name: グリュンフェルト・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black lets White build a big pawn centre, then attacks it with pieces and the g7 bishop: a dynamic, modern defence.
comment.advanced: In the Exchange lines White gets a c3-d4-e4 centre and Black hits d4 with ...Bg7, ...c5 and ...Nc6; very concrete theory, with White's centre and attack against Black's queenside majority.

ja.name: カタラン・オープニング

comment.beginner: White combines the Queen's Gambit with a bishop on g2 that presses on Black's queenside along the long diagonal.
comment.advanced: White gives up or delays the c4 pawn for long-diagonal pressure; Black chooses between the Open (...dxc4) and Closed (...Be7, ...c6) systems, and the endgames often favour White's bishop.

ja.name: ベノニ・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black plays ...c5 and accepts a blocked centre in exchange for a queenside pawn majority: an ambitious, unbalanced defence.
comment.advanced: The Modern Benoni is asymmetrical (White's d5 pawn against ...c5 and ...d6): Black has the queenside majority and the g7 bishop, White the central majority and the e5 break.

ja.name: ベンコー・ギャンビット

comment.beginner: Black gives a queenside pawn to open the a- and b-files for the rooks: long-lasting pressure rather than quick tactics.
comment.advanced: The Benko (Volga) Gambit trades a pawn for permanent queenside pressure (rooks on a8 and b8, bishop on g7), and Black is often happy in an endgame a pawn down.

ja.name: レティ・オープニング

comment.beginner: White develops the knight, then attacks Black's centre from the side with c4: a flexible, hypermodern opening.
comment.advanced: The Réti presses on d5 with c4 and a g2 fianchetto, often transposing to Catalan, English or QGD structures, while the double-fianchetto lines stay independent.

ja.name: キングズ・インディアン・アタック

comment.beginner: White sets up Nf3, g3, Bg2, castling, d3 and e4 against almost anything: a system with a clear kingside plan.
comment.advanced: A King's Indian with colours reversed and an extra tempo; against French or Sicilian setups White plays e5 and attacks the king (h4, Nf1-h2-g4) while Black expands on the queenside.

ja.name: バード・オープニング

comment.beginner: White starts with the f-pawn to control e5: an unusual opening that leads to Dutch positions with the colours reversed.
comment.advanced: White aims for a kingside setup (Nf3, e3, b3 and Bb2, or g3); Black's sharpest answer is From's Gambit, 1...e5.

ja.name: ポンツィアーニ・オープニング

comment.beginner: White prepares d4 with c3 to build a pawn centre: an old and fairly rare opening.
comment.advanced: c3 prepares d4 but takes the knight's best square; Black equalises with the ...Nf6 or ...d5 counterattacks.

es.name: Apertura de los tres caballos
es.def: la apertura de los tres caballos

ja.name: スリー・ナイツ・ゲーム

comment.beginner: White brings out a third knight early; if Black adds the fourth knight, it becomes the Four Knights Game.
comment.advanced: A transpositional move order; Black's independent tries are ...Bb4 and ...g6.

ja.name: デニッシュ・ギャンビット

comment.beginner: White gives one or even two pawns for a big lead in development and two bishops aiming at Black's king.
comment.advanced: Pawns are traded for open lines and bishops on c4 and b2; giving material back with ...d5 is Black's safest way to neutralise it.

ja.name: ブラックマー・ディーマー・ギャンビット

comment.beginner: White sacrifices a pawn with e4 and f3 to open the f-file and attack quickly.
comment.advanced: A pawn for development and the half-open f-file; Black may accept or decline, and theory favours Black if the development is sound.

ja.name: トロンポウスキー・アタック

comment.beginner: White attacks the f6 knight at once with the bishop: an early surprise that takes Black out of the usual paths.
comment.advanced: 2.Bg5 threatens to double Black's pawns; Black answers with ...Ne4, ...e6 or ...c5, leading to unbalanced minor-piece play.

ja.name: トーレ・アタック

comment.beginner: After Nf3 White develops the bishop to g5 to pin the knight and builds a solid centre with e3 and c3.
comment.advanced: A system (d4, Nf3, Bg5, e3, Nbd2, c3) aiming for e4; Black usually replies with ...c5 or an early ...h6.

ja.name: コール・システム

comment.beginner: White builds the pawn triangle d4-e3-c3 with the bishop on d3 and prepares e4: a simple, solid attacking system.
comment.advanced: White prepares e4 for a kingside attack (Colle-Koltanowski) or plays b3 and Bb2 (Colle-Zukertort); the drawback is the passive c1 bishop.

ja.name: タラッシュ・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black plays ...c5 against the Queen's Gambit and accepts an isolated d-pawn in exchange for free piece play.
comment.advanced: Black deliberately takes an isolated queen's pawn for activity; White blockades d5 and fianchettoes with g3, while Black looks for piece play and the ...d4 advance.

ja.name: ブダペスト・ギャンビット

comment.beginner: Black gives the e-pawn against 1.d4 and 2.c4 to develop quickly; the pawn is usually won back.
comment.advanced: After ...e5 and ...Ng4 Black regains the pawn in most lines; White keeps a small edge with Bf4 or e4 setups, and the Fajarowicz (...Ne4) is a trickier sideline.

ja.name: ボゴ・インディアン・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black checks with the bishop on b4 to disturb White's development: a solid, simple defence.
comment.advanced: Usually a bishop trade on d2 or a Nimzo-like structure without the knight pin; Black aims for a solid ...d5 or ...d6 and ...e5 setup.

ja.name: オールド・インディアン・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black plays ...d6 and ...e5 without a fianchetto: a solid, slightly passive defence.
comment.advanced: A King's Indian with the bishop on e7: solid but cramped, with ...e5 and ...Nbd7 central play.

families.note: lichess puts the root at 1.d4 d6 2.c4 (parity would give it to White): the curated side is authoritative.

ja.name: チゴリン・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black develops the queen's knight to c6 against the Queen's Gambit and plays for active pieces.
comment.advanced: Black gives up central pawn solidity for piece activity, often trading the light bishop for the f3 knight to press on d4.

ja.name: アルビン・カウンターギャンビット

comment.beginner: Black counter-sacrifices the e-pawn to push ...d4 and cramp White: sharp and full of traps.
comment.advanced: Black relies on the d4 wedge and fast development (the Lasker Trap is the classic danger); White's best is quiet development with g3 and returning material when needed.

ja.name: ラトビアン・ギャンビット

comment.beginner: Black plays ...f5 on move two: a very risky gambit that weakens Black's own king.
comment.advanced: Objectively dubious: White gets a strong initiative with Nxe5 and Qh5+ ideas or with Bc4.

ja.name: エレファント・ギャンビット

comment.beginner: Black strikes back with ...d5 at once and offers a pawn to open lines: risky but tricky.
comment.advanced: Objectively unsound; after exd5 White keeps a good game with careful development.

families.note: Arabic avoids الفيل (= bishop in Arabic chess) and transliterates.

ja.name: ニムゾ・ラーセン・アタック

comment.beginner: White puts the queen's bishop on the long diagonal with b3 and Bb2 to control e5 and the centre from afar.
comment.advanced: A hypermodern flank setup; Black occupies the centre with ...e5 or ...d5 and White presses on it with Bb2, e3 and f4 or c4.

ja.name: ポーリッシュ・オープニング

comment.beginner: White starts with b4, an unusual wing move that gains space on the queenside.
comment.advanced: The Polish (Sokolsky) puts the bishop on b2 after b4; the b4 pawn can become a target, but the opening is playable and surprising.

ja.name: グロブ・オープニング

comment.beginner: White pushes the g-pawn two squares on move one: a provocative opening that weakens White's own king.
comment.advanced: White aims at the long diagonal with Bg2 and pressure on b7; Black answers with ...d5 and ...e5 and should punish the loosened kingside.

ja.name: ハンガリアン・オープニング

comment.beginner: White prepares a fianchetto with g3 and Bg2: a flexible start that often becomes a King's Indian Attack or an English.
comment.advanced: 1.g3 (Benko's Opening) is highly transpositional: Réti, English and King's Indian Attack setups, or a reversed Modern Defence.

ja.name: ミーゼス・オープニング

comment.beginner: White starts very modestly with d3, opening the c1 bishop without taking the centre.
comment.advanced: 1.d3 often leads to reversed Pirc or King's Indian Attack setups; Black may take the centre freely.

ja.name: サラゴサ・オープニング

comment.beginner: White starts with c3, a very rare and quiet first move.
comment.advanced: 1.c3 prepares a supported d4 and can transpose to reversed Caro-Kann or Slav structures.

ja.name: ファン・ヘート・オープニング

comment.beginner: White develops the queen's knight first, an unusual move that keeps e4 or d4 in reserve.
comment.advanced: The Van Geet (Dunst) often transposes to Vienna, reversed Sicilian or Pirc-type positions.

ja.name: ラポート・ジョバヴァ・システム

comment.beginner: White combines Nc3 and Bf4 against 1...d5: an aggressive system that aims at the c7 square with Nb5.
comment.advanced: White develops Nc3 and Bf4 with ideas of Nb5, e3 and often long castling with an h4 or g4 attack; Black must watch c7 and the e4 advance.

ja.name: ストーンウォール・アタック

comment.beginner: White puts pawns on d4, e3 and f4 and the bishop on d3, aiming for a kingside attack with a knight on e5.
comment.advanced: e5 is firmly controlled and White attacks with Ne5 and Rf3-h3, but e4 and c4 become weak; Black's best is a quick ...c5 or trading the d3 bishop with ...Bf5.

ja.name: リヒター・ヴェレソフ・アタック

comment.beginner: White develops the queen's knight to c3 and the bishop to g5 early, aiming for e4.
comment.advanced: Nc3 blocks the c-pawn but prepares f3 and e4; Black does well with ...Nbd7 and ...c5, or ...Bf5 setups.

ja.name: セント・ジョージ・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black starts with ...a6 and ...b5, a rare wing setup made famous by Miles's win over Karpov in 1980.
comment.advanced: Black aims for ...Bb7 and queenside expansion and gives up the centre; White keeps an edge with simple central development.

ja.name: ボルグ・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black pushes the g-pawn two squares: a provocative opening that weakens Black's own king.
comment.advanced: The Grob with colours reversed; White gains space and time with d4 and ideas of Bxg5.

ja.name: ヒポポタマス・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black puts the pawns on the sixth rank and fianchettoes both bishops, waiting for White to overextend.
comment.advanced: A flexible waiting setup (...g6, ...b6, ...e6, ...d6, ...Nd7, ...Ne7): sound against slow play, cramped against a broad centre.

families.note: lichess only names the rare 1...Nh6 move order; the setup itself is usually reached through Modern or Owen move orders.

ja.name: イングリッシュ・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black answers with ...b6 and ...Bb7 to fight for e4 with pieces.
comment.advanced: The English Defence (...e6, ...b6) invites a big centre, then attacks it with ...Bb4, ...f5 and pressure on e4.

ja.name: プテロダクティル・ディフェンス

comment.beginner: Black fianchettoes the king's bishop and plays ...c5 and ...Qa5 early: an offbeat, aggressive system.
comment.advanced: A mix of Modern and Sicilian ideas: ...g6, ...Bg7, ...c5 and ...Qa5, hitting the c3 knight along the a5-e1 diagonal.

ja.name: ボングクラウド・アタック

comment.beginner: White moves the king on move two: a joke opening that breaks the basic rules, since the king should stay safe and castle.
comment.advanced: 2.Ke2 blocks the bishop and the queen and gives up castling; it is played as a meme and should not be imitated.

lichess: Sicilian Defense: Modern Variations, Main Line

names.ja: オープン・シシリアン

comment.advanced: White opens the centre with d4 and recaptures with the knight: the main battleground of the Sicilian, sharp and heavy with theory.

names.ja: クローズド・シシリアン

comment.advanced: White avoids d4 and plays Nc3, g3, Bg2 and often f4, aiming for a slow kingside attack.

names.ja: アラピン・バリエーション

comment.advanced: 2.c3 prepares d4 to build a full pawn centre and sidestep the main Sicilian theory; Black answers with ...d5 or ...Nf6.

names.ja: スミス・モラ・ギャンビット

comment.advanced: A pawn for rapid development and the open c- and d-files; Black develops soundly and often returns the pawn at the right moment.
comment.beginner: White gives a pawn to develop quickly and open lines against Black's king: Black must develop carefully.

names.ja: グランプリ・アタック

comment.advanced: White plays Nc3 and f4 for a quick kingside attack with f5, avoiding the Open Sicilian.

names.ja: ロッソリモ・バリエーション

comment.advanced: 3.Bb5 pins or trades the c6 knight to give Black doubled pawns and keep the game positional.

names.ja: ナイドルフ・バリエーション

comment.advanced: 5...a6 is the most famous Sicilian: flexible and deep, with ...e5 or ...e6 structures against sharp attacks such as the English Attack or 6.Bg5.

names.ja: ドラゴン・バリエーション

comment.advanced: Black fianchettoes to g7 (the pawn chain looks like a dragon); the Yugoslav Attack leads to famous races of attacks on opposite wings.

lichess: Sicilian Defense: Dragon Variation, Accelerated Dragon

names.ja: アクセラレーテッド・ドラゴン

comment.advanced: Black fianchettoes before ...d6 to play ...d5 in one go; the Maróczy Bind with c4 is White's positional antidote.

names.ja: シェベニンゲン・バリエーション

comment.advanced: Black builds the small centre e6-d6, a flexible defensive shell; White often attacks with g4 (the Keres Attack).

names.ja: スヴェシニコフ・バリエーション

comment.advanced: Black plays ...e5, accepting a hole on d5 and a backward d-pawn for activity and the bishop pair: very dynamic.

notable_variations.note: lichess calls the whole 5...e5 system "Lasker-Pelikan Variation" and only the 7.Bg5 a6 8.Na3 b5 main line "Sveshnikov Variation".

names.ja: タイマノフ・バリエーション

comment.advanced: Black combines ...e6 and ...Nc6 with a flexible ...a6 and ...Qc7, keeping ...d6 or ...Bb4 in reserve.

names.ja: カン・バリエーション

comment.advanced: Black plays ...e6 and ...a6, keeps the knights at home and often aims for a Hedgehog setup.

names.ja: クラシカル・バリエーション

comment.advanced: Black develops both knights (...Nc6, ...Nf6, ...d6); White's main answers are the Richter-Rauzer (Bg5) and the Sozin (Bc4).

names.ja: アドバンス・バリエーション

comment.advanced: White locks the centre with e5 and gains space; Black attacks d4, the base of the chain, with ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Qb6.

names.ja: エクスチェンジ・バリエーション

comment.advanced: exd5 releases the tension: a symmetrical, quiet structure in which Black's light bishop is freed.

names.ja: タラッシュ・バリエーション

comment.advanced: 3.Nd2 avoids the Winawer pin; Black often accepts an isolated d-pawn after ...c5 or plays ...Nf6 for a locked centre.

names.ja: ウィナワー・バリエーション

comment.advanced: 3...Bb4 pins the knight; after e5 and a3 Black usually gives bishop for knight, leaving White doubled c-pawns but the bishop pair and kingside chances.

names.ja: クラシカル・バリエーション

comment.advanced: 3...Nf6 invites 4.Bg5 or 4.e5; the play turns on the e5 chain and the f6 knight.

names.ja: ルビンシュタイン・バリエーション

comment.advanced: 3...dxe4 gives up the centre for a solid, compact position; Black aims for ...Nd7, ...Ngf6 and ...c5.

names.ja: アドバンス・バリエーション

comment.advanced: White gains space with e5; Black develops the bishop to f5 before ...e6 and fights back with ...c5.

names.ja: エクスチェンジ・バリエーション

comment.advanced: A Carlsbad structure with colours reversed: White usually plays Bd3, c3 and a kingside setup, Black a minority attack with ...b5-b4.

names.ja: パノフ・アタック

comment.advanced: White plays c4 and accepts an isolated d-pawn in exchange for active pieces and attacking chances.

names.ja: クラシカル・バリエーション

comment.advanced: 4...Bf5 develops the bishop with tempo on the e4 knight; White gains space with h4-h5 and castling on opposite sides is common.

names.ja: ツー・ナイツ・アタック

comment.advanced: White develops Nc3 and Nf3 before d4, staying flexible and avoiding main-line theory.

names.ja: ツー・ナイツ・ディフェンス

comment.advanced: 3...Nf6 invites the sharp 4.Ng5 (answered by ...d5 and ...Na5) or the quiet 4.d3; it is Black's most active reply to the Italian.
comment.beginner: Black counterattacks e4 with the knight instead of copying White; watch out for Ng5, which hits f7.

names.ja: ジュオッコ・ピアノ

comment.advanced: 3...Bc5 mirrors White's bishop; White chooses between c3 and d4 central play, the slow d3 (Pianissimo) or the Evans Gambit.
comment.beginner: "The quiet game" in Italian: both bishops aim at the opponent's f-pawn and the game develops calmly.

lichess: Italian Game: Classical Variation, Giuoco Pianissimo

names.ja: ジュオッコ・ピアニッシモ

comment.advanced: The modern slow Italian (d3, c3, castling, Re1, a4, h3): long manoeuvres like Nbd2-f1-g3 and a delayed d4 break.

names.ja: エバンス・ギャンビット

comment.advanced: 4.b4 gives a pawn to deflect the c5 bishop and build a fast centre with c3 and d4: very sharp, a favourite of the romantic era.

lichess: Italian Game: Two Knights Defense, Fried Liver Attack

names.ja: フライド・リバー・アタック

comment.advanced: After 4.Ng5 d5 5.exd5 Nxd5?! 6.Nxf7 Kxf7 White gets a fierce attack; the main line 5...Na5 avoids it.
comment.beginner: White sacrifices the knight on f7 to drag Black's king into the open: very dangerous if Black recaptured on d5 with the knight.

lichess: Italian Game: Two Knights Defense, Traxler Counterattack
Italian Game: Two Knights Defense, Traxler Variation

names.ja: トラクスラー・カウンターアタック

comment.advanced: 4...Bc5 ignores the threat to f7 and hits f2 instead: wild tactics where exact knowledge decides.

names.ja: ベルリン・ディフェンス

comment.advanced: 3...Nf6 counterattacks e4; the famous Berlin endgame (queens off early, Black's king in the centre) is extremely solid.

names.ja: モーフィー・ディフェンス

comment.advanced: 3...a6 questions the bishop at once: the gateway to the main lines (Closed, Open, Marshall).

names.ja: クローズド・ルイ・ロペス

comment.advanced: 5...Be7 with ...b5, ...d6 and castling: the classical main line, with slow manoeuvres (Nbd2-f1-g3) against Black's queenside plans (Breyer, Zaitsev, Chigorin).

names.ja: マーシャル・アタック

comment.advanced: 8...d5 sacrifices a pawn for a lasting kingside attack; deeply analysed, it is a respected drawing weapon at the top level.

names.ja: エクスチェンジ・バリエーション

comment.advanced: 4.Bxc6 gives Black the bishop pair but doubled c-pawns; White aims for an endgame with a healthy kingside majority.

names.ja: オープン・バリエーション

comment.advanced: 5...Nxe4 takes the centre pawn for active piece play; Black's pieces are lively but the e-file and the d5 pawn need care.

names.ja: シュリーマン・ディフェンス

comment.advanced: 3...f5 is a King's Gambit with the colours reversed: sharp and risky for both sides.

names.ja: スコッチ・ギャンビット

comment.advanced: White plays Bc4 instead of recapturing on d4 and offers a pawn for fast development; it often transposes to the Two Knights.

names.ja: ウィーン・ギャンビット

comment.advanced: f4 in the Vienna, a King's Gambit with Nc3 already played; Black's best answer is the central strike ...d5.

names.ja: スタッフォード・ギャンビット

comment.advanced: After 3.Nxe5 Nc6 4.Nxc6 dxc6 Black gets quick development and traps with ...Bc5 and ...Ng4; with calm moves (d3, Be2, castling) White stays a clean pawn up.
comment.beginner: A trap-filled gambit popular online: Black gives a pawn and hopes White falls for tricks against f2 and e4.

lichess: King's Pawn Game: Wayward Queen Attack

names.ja: ウェイワード・クイーン・アタック

comment.advanced: 2.Qh5 (or 2.Qf3) breaks the rule of early development; Black gains time by harassing the queen (...Nc6, ...g6, ...Nf6) and should come out better.
comment.beginner: An early queen raid aiming at f7, the idea of Scholar's Mate: defend with ...Nc6 and ...g6 or ...Qe7, then chase the queen with your pieces.

notable_variations.note: "Wayward Queen Attack" has no settled translation; the proposal uses the alternative English name "Parham Attack" in fr/de/es/ru/uk.

names.ja: ハロウィン・ギャンビット

comment.advanced: 4.Nxe5 gives a knight for two pawns and a big centre: objectively unsound but dangerous in fast games.

names.ja: オーソドックス・ディフェンス

comment.advanced: The classical setup (...Be7, castling, ...Nbd7): solid but passive, freed by ...dxc4 with ...e5 or ...c5 (Capablanca's freeing manoeuvre).

names.ja: エクスチェンジ・バリエーション

comment.advanced: cxd5 exd5 creates the Carlsbad structure; White's classic plan is the minority attack b4-b5 against Black's c6 pawn.

names.ja: セミタラッシュ・ディフェンス

comment.advanced: ...c5 with the knight on f6 recaptures on d5 with a piece and avoids the isolated pawn of the Tarrasch; White gets a mobile centre.

names.ja: メラン・バリエーション

comment.advanced: ...dxc4 and ...b5 gain queenside space with tempo; the play turns on the ...c5 break and White's e4-e5 push.

names.ja: クラシカル・バリエーション

comment.advanced: Nf3, Be2 and castling: after ...e5 and d5 the famous race begins, White on the queenside (c5), Black on the kingside (...f5, ...f4, ...g5).

names.ja: ゼーミッシュ・バリエーション

comment.advanced: f3 supports e4 and prepares Be3, Qd2 and a kingside pawn storm; Black answers with ...c5, ...e5 or the ...Nc6, ...a6, ...b5 plan.

lichess: King's Indian Defense: Four Pawns Attack

names.ja: フォー・ポーンズ・アタック

comment.advanced: White builds a c4-d4-e4-f4 wall; Black undermines it at once with ...c5 and ...e6, leading to Benoni-like tactics.

names.ja: フィアンケット・バリエーション

comment.advanced: g3 and Bg2 blunt the g7 bishop; the game is more positional, with ...Nc6 and ...a6 or ...c6 and ...Qb6 plans for Black.

names.ja: ルビンシュタイン・バリエーション

comment.advanced: 4.e3 develops calmly and keeps Bd3, Ne2 or a3 in reserve: the most popular way to meet the Nimzo.

names.ja: クラシカル・バリエーション

comment.advanced: 4.Qc2 avoids doubled pawns by recapturing on c3 with the queen; White gets the bishop pair, Black fast development.

names.ja: ゼーミッシュ・バリエーション

comment.advanced: 4.a3 forces ...Bxc3+ at once; White accepts doubled c-pawns for the bishop pair and a big centre.

names.ja: エクスチェンジ・バリエーション

comment.advanced: cxd5 and e4 build the big centre; Black attacks d4 with ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Bg4, and the endgames often favour Black's queenside majority.

notable_variations.note: lichess's shortest line ends with 4...Nxd5, so plain parity would credit Black: the curated side (White) is authoritative.

names.ja: レニングラード・バリエーション

comment.advanced: ...g6 and ...Bg7: a King's Indian-style Dutch in which Black plays for ...e5 and kingside play.

names.ja: ストーンウォール・バリエーション

comment.advanced: Pawns on c6, d5, e6 and f5 give Black a rock-solid grip on e4, at the cost of a hole on e5 and a passive light bishop.

names.ja: モダン・ベノニ

comment.advanced: ...e6 and ...exd5 give Black a queenside majority against White's central majority; tactics around e5 and the g7 bishop dominate.

names.ja: オープン・カタラン

comment.advanced: ...dxc4 takes the pawn; White wins it back with Qc2 or Qa4 and keeps long-diagonal pressure, Black aims for ...c5 or ...b5 and ...Bb7.

notable_variations.note: lichess's shortest line ends with 4.Bg2 (parity: White); the choice of ...dxc4 is Black's.

names.ja: クローズド・カタラン

comment.advanced: Black keeps d5 with ...Be7, ...c6 and ...Nbd7: a slow positional fight around the ...e5 or ...b6 and ...Bb7 freeing plans.

names.ja: シンメトリカル・バリエーション

comment.advanced: 1...c5 copies White: slow manoeuvring with fianchettoes, pressure on d4 and d5, and Hedgehog or Maróczy-type structures.

names.ja: リバースド・シシリアン

comment.advanced: 1...e5 turns the English into a Sicilian with an extra tempo for White; typical plans are g3 and Bg2 with d3 and a queenside push.

names.ja: フォー・ポーンズ・アタック

comment.advanced: White chases the knight with c4, e5 and f4 and builds a huge but overextended centre; Black counters with ...dxe5, ...c5 and ...Bf5.

names.ja: モダン・バリエーション

comment.advanced: 4.Nf3 keeps a solid space advantage without overextending; Black pins with ...Bg4 or fianchettoes with ...g6.

names.ja: オーストリアン・アタック

comment.advanced: f4 builds a big centre for e5 or a kingside attack; Black strikes with ...c5, or castles and plays ...c5 or ...e5.

names.ja: ファルクビア・カウンターギャンビット

comment.advanced: 2...d5 strikes back in the centre instead of taking on f4; modern practice favours 3.exd5 with ...exf4 or ...e4 lines.
